title: The Clock That Solved the Deadliest Problem at Sea

segments.text: Over fourteen hundred sailors died because nobody knew what time it was.
Seventeen-oh-seven. A British fleet is lost in thick fog.
Sailors could tell how far north they were. But east or west? Pure guesswork.
So Britain offered a prize. Twenty thousand pounds. Millions today.
The secret was time. Carry the exact time from home, compare it to the sun, and you know where you are.
But no clock could survive a rolling, salty ship. Experts said it was impossible.
Then came John Harrison. A carpenter with no formal training.
He spent decades building giant sea clocks.
Then he realised he'd been thinking too big.
His fourth timekeeper fit in your hand.
Eighty-one days at sea to Jamaica. It was only five seconds off.
And the experts still refused to pay him.
It took the King himself before Harrison finally got his money.
